  • Siberian Yupik↗Documented language community geography
    Connection & source
    Documented language community geography

    The university profile identifies St. Lawrence Island villages and explicitly discusses Siberian Yupik people in Alaska. This Alaska connection does not conflate Siberian Yupik with Central Alaskan Yup'ik; dated speaker totals are excluded.

    Public content inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Sugpiaq↗People name / traditional regional connection
    Connection & source
    People name / traditional regional connection

    The community museum identifies Alutiiq/Sugpiaq people with southcentral Alaska, including Prince William Sound, the outer Kenai Peninsula, Kodiak and the Alaska Peninsula. Its naming lesson explains community variation in use of Sugpiaq and Alutiiq. These overlapping access names do not denote two wholly separate nations, and neither is interchangeable with the Unangan of the Aleutian Islands. Inspection: Actual opening identity/geography paragraphs and naming lesson, especially community-specific name usage.

    Undated museum educational account; inspected October 21, 2026. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Tanana↗Language community geographic association
    Connection & source
    Language community geographic association

    The Tanana language introduction locates its language communities at Nenana and Minto on the Tanana River below Fairbanks. The page's acknowledgement identifies Lower Tanana Dene stewardship at Troth Yeddha'. Inspection: Opening geographic paragraph and publication paragraph; Lower Tanana land acknowledgement. Limits: This is the page's Lower Tanana scope, not all Tanana River peoples or Upper Tanana. Undated speaker/population totals not adopted.

    Undated language introduction, inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Tlingit↗Historical homeland / community government connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland / community government connection

    The Council's timeline explicitly identifies Tlingit and Haida as distinct nations and repeatedly locates the historical land-use and claims account in Southeast Alaska. Supports Alaska for the Tlingit directory entry; this joint Council does not stand for every Tlingit community or the full cross-border homeland.

    Historical Southeast Alaska geography in the joint Council's public timeline. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Tsimshian↗Historical migration / language community connection
    Connection & source
    Historical migration / language community connection

    The Center locates Tsimshian at Metlakatla on Annette Island in southeastern Alaska and dates the movement from Canada to 1887. Inspection: Opening geographic paragraph and orthography paragraph. Limits: One Alaska Tsimshian community and its language history; not the whole Tsimshian homeland or all Tsimshian governments. Undated speaker figures excluded.

    Metlakatla, Alaska, from the 1887 migration onward. Reviewed 2026-10-21.
